documentation.range: Notropis aulidion was historically restricted to the Rio del Tunal in the upper Rio Mezquital drainage basin, Durango, Mexico (Chernoff and Miller 1986, Miller et al. 1989, Miller et al. 2005). It was known from only two collections in a small reservoir (Miller et al. 2005). It was last recorded in 1961 despite multiple subsequent sampling attempts, and is now widely regarded as extinct (Miller et al. 2005, Jelks et al. 2008, Bennett and Conway 2010, Burkhead 2012).
documentation.population: The historical population size of this species is unknown. It has not been reported since 1961 (Miller et al. 1989). Many surveys in the species' historical range and nearby areas have not reported the species.
documentation.habitats: The historical habitat of this species was restricted to a single narrow reservoir at an elevation of 1865 m Asl, with minimal vegetation, a muddy substrate, low velocity flow and a water depth of 1 m (Miller et al. 1989, 2005).
documentation.threats: The extirpation of this species likely resulted from reduced streamflow, municipal and industrial pollution, and the effects of introduced nonnative species (e.g. Micropterus salmoides) following marked increases in the population and development of Durango City (Miller et al. 1989).
documentation.measures: There are no species-specific conservation measures in place for N. aulidion as it is considered extinct.
documentation.use_trade: The historical use and trade of this species is unknown.
documentation.rationale: Notropis aulidion was historically known only from a long, narrow reservoir of the Rio del Tunal in the upper Rio Mezquital drainage basin, Durango, Mexico. Despite extensive sampling attempts, this species was last recorded in 1961 and is now widely regarded as Extinct.
